name: St Kitts and Nevis
intro: St Kitts and Nevis are two islands that share one set of records. Early registers were lost to war, fire and hurricanes, so what survives starts later than on some islands: church baptisms from 1716, and civil registration from 1859. Our St Kitts, Nevis and Anguilla research group, for members, meets at Solihull Core Library and on Zoom.

parish_note: St Kitts has nine parishes and Nevis has five. Many parish names include their main village, such as St Thomas Middle Island.
parish_tip: Church of England registers for {parish} are among the St Kitts and Nevis church records on FamilySearch. The images can only be viewed at a FamilySearch centre or an affiliate library such as Solihull Core Library.

resources.title: FamilySearch
resources.text: Free. Civil registration from 1859 to 1932 and Church of England records from 1747 to 1930. You can search the indexes at home, but the images of the registers can only be viewed at a FamilySearch centre or an affiliate library.
resources.link: Search St Kitts and Nevis on FamilySearch
resources.check: Confirm which collections can be viewed at home.

resources.title: At Solihull Core Library
resources.text: Our St Kitts, Nevis and Anguilla group meets at the library because the register images can be viewed there. Solihull Libraries also list the Caribbean family history films they hold.
resources.link: See the library's list of films

resources.title: National Archives of St Kitts and Nevis
resources.text: In Basseterre. Holds government records, registers and newspapers for both islands. Write before you visit.

resources.title: Nevis Historical and Conservation Society
resources.text: In Charlestown. Its archive and library cover Nevis families, estates and churches.
resources.link: Visit the Nevis Historical and Conservation Society

resources.title: Slave registers and compensation records
resources.text: Registers of enslaved people made between 1817 and 1834, at The National Archives (series T 71), and searchable on Ancestry. The Legacies of British Slavery database at UCL covers the owners and estates paid compensation.

resources.title: Findmypast
resources.text: Baptisms from some St Kitts and Nevis parishes, 1716 to 1881, indexed by name. A subscription site, free to use in many libraries.

looking.label: Where they lived or owned land

records.title: Civil registration
records.why: Births and deaths were registered from 1859 on St Kitts and from 1861 on Nevis. Marriage indexes begin in 1885 on St Kitts and 1905 on Nevis.
records.where: FamilySearch (free): search the index at home, and view the registers at Solihull Core Library.

records.title: Church of England registers
records.why: Baptisms, marriages and burials. Dates differ by parish and there are gaps, because early registers were lost to war, fire and hurricanes.
records.where: FamilySearch and Findmypast; view the images at Solihull Core Library.

records.title: Methodist and Moravian registers
records.why: Many enslaved and free Black families were baptised and married by the Methodist and Moravian missions, not the parish church.
records.where: Ask us: some are with the churches and some at the National Archives in Basseterre.

records.title: Slave registers, 1817 to 1834
records.why: Every few years, owners had to list the people they enslaved, with names, ages, colour and country of birth. They can link a family across a generation.
records.where: The National Archives (T 71), searchable on Ancestry.

records.title: Compensation records and estate histories
records.why: When slavery was abolished, owners, not the enslaved, were paid compensation. The records name estates, which helps you find where an enslaved ancestor lived.
records.where: Legacies of British Slavery database, UCL (free).

records.title: Wills and deeds
records.why: Wills name family and property; deeds record land changing hands.
records.where: The National Archives of St Kitts and Nevis, Basseterre.

records.title: Passenger lists to the UK, 1878 to 1960
records.why: Ships arriving in Britain listed every passenger, including the Windrush generation, often with an age, job and address.
records.where: The National Archives (BT 26), searchable on Ancestry and Findmypast.

records.title: British Army and the West India Regiment
records.why: Many Kittitians and Nevisians served in the West India Regiments from 1795, and in the British West Indies Regiment in the First World War. Service records give birthplaces and families.
records.where: The National Archives; many on Findmypast and Ancestry.

finder.always: Start with what your family knows, then work back one generation at a time. Bring what you find to a meeting: someone has usually been stuck in the same place.

timeline.label: Slavery is abolished. Apprenticeship follows until 1838.
Civil registration begins on St Kitts. Nevis follows in 1861.
St Kitts, Nevis and Anguilla are joined as one presidency.
